label: Riser Doors
summary: Fire-rated steel access doors to service risers and shafts, supplied and installed.
construction: Steel doorset with insulated core, supplied pre-hung with multi-point locking. Exact construction follows the doorset matched to the stated requirement and is confirmed on the order drawing.
_PROVISIONAL: INTERNAL NOTE — never rendered in the interface or the PDF. This file describes the riser door CATEGORY: what the customer can ask for. Which supplier product fulfils a given requirement is resolved by lib/riserMatch.js against data/riser-door-suppliers.json and data/fire-test-reports.json — supplier identities never reach the customer. The statedLimits here are the UNION across suppliers (they drive input hints and the bespoke-enquiry wording); per-supplier limits live in the suppliers file. clearOpening here is indicative only, used when no supplier match exists; matched resolutions carry the matched product's own deductions. Still unconfirmed: whether E and EI classifications are offered (neither held test report states any EN 13501-2 classification), and the height deductions for the two newer supplier products.

statedLimits.source: Union of supplier envelopes. Leaf count capped at 4 — the largest configuration any supplier manufactures (quad door).

clearOpening.note: Indicative clear opening — the exact frame deduction depends on the doorset matched to the requirement and is confirmed on the order drawing.

structuralAllowance.note: Prepare the structural opening slightly larger than the ordered door; adjustable frames take up the tolerance, so no packers or mastic are needed.

fireClassificationNote: EW adds control of radiated heat to integrity, reducing the risk of fire spreading by radiation and allowing safer passage past an open riser door on an escape route. Fire integrity is bi-directionally tested; the sheet states exactly what the held test evidence covers.

options.label: Handing
options.note: Viewed from the access side. For multi-leaf sets this is the active leaf.

options.label: Wall construction
options.note: The fire rating depends on the partition meeting the required fire performance. Wall construction also guides the frame profile below.

choices.label: Deep plaster frame
choices.note: Suits wet plastering / float and set.

choices.label: Euro-cylinder and concealed keyhole
choices.note: Most popular — handles are rarely fitted to flush doors.

choices.label: Concealed keyhole only
choices.note: Square-drive T-key. The keyhole sits behind a spring-loaded flap.

choices.label: Euro-cylinder only
choices.note: Cylinder visible; the last turn of the key operates the latch.

choices.label: Fully concealed
choices.note: Keyhole and euro-cylinder both behind a magnet-held flush flap.

choices.label: High-security three-point lock
choices.note: Euro profile cylinder with secondary locking, engaging top, bottom and lock sides.

options.label: Acoustic requirement
options.note: State the rating the Acoustic Report asks for; sound-rated doorsets need certified perimeter and threshold seals.

options.label: Smoke control
options.note: Smoke-sealed doorsets carry tested compression seals in addition to the intumescent fire seals.

options.label: Riser guardrails
options.note: Two demountable horizontal tubular guardrails are the standard provision behind riser doors on most project specifications.

choices.label: Low-resin powder for over-painting
choices.note: Formulated to take emulsion and blend into the surrounding wall. No extra cost.
